chunks: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq - may God have Mercy upon him - narrated that Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Hamadani quoted on the authority of Ali ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faz'al, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Musa Ar-Rida (peace be upon him) that he said:
We are the Masters in this world and the Rulers in the Hereafter.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and political status of the Imams according to Imam Ar-Rida?
ai.summary: In this tradition from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, Imam al-Rida (a.s.) articulates the dual nature of the Ahl al-Bayt's authority, distinguishing between their political and social mastery in this world and their spiritual sovereignty in the Hereafter. This statement underscores the Shia belief that the Imams are not merely spiritual guides but also possess inherent leadership (*Sidq*) that manifests in both temporal and eternal realms, fulfilling the promise of divine vicegerency.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 31-210 Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq - may God have Mercy upon him - narrated that Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa’eed al-Hamadani quoted on the authority of Ali ibn Al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Faz’zal, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ali ibn Musa Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.), “
We are the ones who are the Masters in this world and the Rulers in the Hereafter.”
